title: Caring for the poor and needy

opening.text: Picture a long table with an empty chair. Someone set that chair on purpose. They hoped a person without a meal would sit there. Caring for the poor and needy is setting that chair. It says, “There is room for you.”

mainMessage.text: Caring for the poor and needy is making room at the table for those who lack.

blocks.text: **He loved them first** Jesus Christ didn't care about the poor as an afterthought. It was a part of His ministry from the start.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Are We Not All Beggars?” from the October 2014 general conference.
From the beginning of His ministry, Jesus loved the impoverished and the disadvantaged in an extraordinary way.
He set the first chair.
**Our own responsibility** The chair is not set by someone else. It is set by each of us.

And also, ye yourselves will succor those that stand in need of your succor; ye will administer of your substance unto him that standeth in need; and ye will not suffer that the beggar putteth up his petition to you in vain, and turn him out to perish.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
As followers of the Savior, we have a personal responsibility to care for the poor and needy.
It is personal.
**Share what you have** No one has to give everything. We give what we have, rich or poor.

And now, for the sake of these things which I have spoken unto you—that is, for the sake of retaining a remission of your sins from day to day, that ye may walk guiltless before God—I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor, every man according to that which he hath, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, visiting the sick and administering to their relief, both spiritually and temporally, according to their wants.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Are We Not All Beggars?” from the October 2014 general conference.
Rich or poor, we are to ‘do what we can’ when others are in need.
Give what you have.
**A loan to the Lord** When we feed one hungry person, we are doing the Lord's work.
He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Caring for the poor and needy is inherent in the ministry of the Savior.
It is His work.
**We all need help** At this table, everyone is a guest. We all depend on God.

For behold, are we not all beggars? Do we not all depend upon the same Being, even God, for all the substance which we have, for both food and raiment, and for gold, and for silver, and for all the riches which we have of every kind?

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Caring for the poor and needy is a fundamental gospel doctrine and an essential element in the eternal plan of salvation.
We are all guests.
**Bread from the fast** The Lord gave us a simple way to fill the table. We fast, and we give.

Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Central to the Lord’s plan for caring for the poor and needy is the law of the fast.
Fast and give.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone helped them in a time of need, or when they helped someone else. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The good Samaritan

blocks.text: A man was hurt and left on the road. Others walked past. A Samaritan stopped.

But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
He saw the man, felt for him and acted. He gave his time, his oil and his money. Compassion becomes real when it moves our feet.

application.text: First, think of one family or person who may be struggling. Second, ask what they need most. Third, give something, even a small thing, and give your fast offering with a glad heart.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know Jesus Christ loves the poor and the needy. I know Heavenly Father hears their prayers, and often answers them through us. I know when we give, our hearts grow. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think of one family or person who may be struggling.
I invite you to ask what they need most.
I invite you to give something, even a small thing, and give your fast offering with a glad heart.
blessings: Someone in need will be helped.
You will feel joy in giving.
You will serve the Savior as you serve them.

closingVerse.text: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:

opening.text: On a cold morning, a coat does a very simple thing. It keeps one person warm. Now think of a coat given away. Someone who was shivering is warm because someone else took off theirs. Caring for the poor and needy often looks just like that. It is plain and personal, and it makes a real difference.

mainMessage.text: Caring for the poor and needy is giving the coat, so someone else can be warm.

blocks.text: **The Savior wore the same cold** Jesus Christ grew up among the poor. He knows what it is to need.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Are We Not All Beggars?” from the October 2014 general conference.
From the beginning of His ministry, Jesus loved the impoverished and the disadvantaged in an extraordinary way.
He knows the cold.
**Yours to give** No one else can hand over your coat. It is a personal choice.

And also, ye yourselves will succor those that stand in need of your succor; ye will administer of your substance unto him that standeth in need; and ye will not suffer that the beggar putteth up his petition to you in vain, and turn him out to perish.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
As followers of the Savior, we have a personal responsibility to care for the poor and needy.
It is yours to give.
**Not the best coat, just a coat** We don't wait until we have more. We give what we have now.

And now, for the sake of these things which I have spoken unto you—that is, for the sake of retaining a remission of your sins from day to day, that ye may walk guiltless before God—I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor, every man according to that which he hath, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, visiting the sick and administering to their relief, both spiritually and temporally, according to their wants.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Are We Not All Beggars?” from the October 2014 general conference.
Rich or poor, we are to ‘do what we can’ when others are in need.
Give what you have.
**Warmth comes back** What we give to those in need, we give to the Lord. He does not forget it.
He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Caring for the poor and needy is inherent in the ministry of the Savior.
It is His work.
**We all wear borrowed warmth** Every one of us depends on God for what we have. That makes us equals.

For behold, are we not all beggars? Do we not all depend upon the same Being, even God, for all the substance which we have, for both food and raiment, and for gold, and for silver, and for all the riches which we have of every kind?

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Caring for the poor and needy is a fundamental gospel doctrine and an essential element in the eternal plan of salvation.
We all depend on God.
**A plan for every coat** The Lord gave us a way so that no coat is given alone. We fast, and we give.

Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Central to the Lord’s plan for caring for the poor and needy is the law of the fast.
Follow His plan.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a small gift meant a lot. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The widow's mites

blocks.text: A poor widow dropped two small coins into the treasury. It was almost nothing.

And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing. And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:
Jesus Christ didn't count the coins. He saw her heart. A small gift, given freely, is large in His eyes.

application.text: First, look at what you own that someone else may need. Second, choose one thing to give this week. Third, pass it on quietly and don't wait to be thanked.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior sees every small gift. I know Heavenly Father blesses those who share. I know giving brings a joy that keeping never can. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to look at what you own that someone else may need.
I invite you to choose one thing to give this week.
I invite you to pass it on quietly and not wait to be thanked.
blessings: You will give as the Savior gives.

closingVerse.text: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

opening.text: A river doesn't keep its water. It receives from the mountains and passes it on to the valley. Fields turn green along its banks. A river that stopped giving would turn into a swamp. Our blessings are like that. They come to us so they can flow on to others.

mainMessage.text: We are rivers, not ponds. What God gives us is meant to flow to those in need.

blocks.text: **The source** The Savior is the source. He loved the poor from the start of His ministry.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Are We Not All Beggars?” from the October 2014 general conference.
From the beginning of His ministry, Jesus loved the impoverished and the disadvantaged in an extraordinary way.
Start at the source.
**Our stretch of the river** Every river has many stretches. Each of us is responsible for ours.

And also, ye yourselves will succor those that stand in need of your succor; ye will administer of your substance unto him that standeth in need; and ye will not suffer that the beggar putteth up his petition to you in vain, and turn him out to perish.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
As followers of the Savior, we have a personal responsibility to care for the poor and needy.
Tend your stretch.
**Whatever the size of the stream** A small stream still waters a field. Rich or poor, we give what we can.

And now, for the sake of these things which I have spoken unto you—that is, for the sake of retaining a remission of your sins from day to day, that ye may walk guiltless before God—I would that ye should impart of your substance to the poor, every man according to that which he hath, such as feeding the hungry, clothing the naked, visiting the sick and administering to their relief, both spiritually and temporally, according to their wants.
Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Are We Not All Beggars?” from the October 2014 general conference.
Rich or poor, we are to ‘do what we can’ when others are in need.
A small stream still helps.
**The water returns** Rain falls, rivers run, and water comes back around. What we give to the poor, the Lord treasures.
He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Caring for the poor and needy is inherent in the ministry of the Savior.
It comes back around.
**Every drop is borrowed** The river never made its own water. We didn't make ours either.

For behold, are we not all beggars? Do we not all depend upon the same Being, even God, for all the substance which we have, for both food and raiment, and for gold, and for silver, and for all the riches which we have of every kind?

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Caring for the poor and needy is a fundamental gospel doctrine and an essential element in the eternal plan of salvation.
All of it is borrowed.
**A channel the Lord dug** A river needs a channel. The Lord gave us one. It is the law of the fast.

Is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry, and that thou bring the poor that are cast out to thy house? when thou seest the naked, that thou cover him; and that thou hide not thyself from thine own flesh?

Bishop Dean M. Davies, Second Counselor in the Presiding Bishopric, said this in his talk “The Law of the Fast: A Personal Responsibility to Care for the Poor and Needy” from the October 2014 general conference.
Central to the Lord’s plan for caring for the poor and needy is the law of the fast.
Use the channel.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they chose to share instead of keep. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Zacchaeus

blocks.text: Zacchaeus was a rich man. When he met Jesus Christ, something changed.
And Zacchæus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
He didn't wait to be asked. After meeting the Savior, he wanted to give. Coming to Christ opens a hand that was closed.

application.text: First, think about what has flowed into your life this year. Second, decide what part could flow out to someone else. Third, pass it on before the month ends.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know everything good comes from God. I know He wants it to flow through us to others. I know Jesus Christ opens hands and hearts. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to think about what has flowed into your life this year.
I invite you to decide what part could flow out to someone else.
I invite you to pass it on before the month ends.
blessings: You will see how much you have received.
You will serve God as you serve your fellow beings.

closingVerse.text: And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.

mainMessage.text: Caring for the poor and needy is leaving a lamp lit for those who walk in the dark.

blocks.text: **The Light first shone** Jesus Christ is the Light. He loved the poor from the first day of His ministry.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.

**Oil in the lamp** What we give is like oil. It keeps the lamp going, and the Lord notices.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a community made sure no one went without. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Early disciples share

blocks.text: The first disciples looked after each other. No one in the group was left in need.

Neither was there any among them that lacked: for as many as were possessors of lands or houses sold them, and brought the prices of the things that were sold, And laid them down at the apostles’ feet: and distribution was made unto every man according as he had need.
They gave freely and shared out fairly. A caring community is a lamp that many hands keep lit.

application.text: First, notice who around you might be walking in the dark. Second, think of one way to leave a light on for them. Third, do it, and keep doing it.

You will become a source of light.

closingVerse.text: For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.

mainMessage.text: Caring for the poor and needy is stitching many small gifts into one warm cover.

blocks.text: **The Savior's own hands** Jesus Christ gave His own life to the poor and the lowly. He started the quilt.

He started the quilt.

Pick up the needle.

Use what you have.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when many people gave a little and it added up to a lot. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The people of the church

blocks.text: The Nephite church members gave to those in need, and they didn't count the cost.

And they did impart of their substance, every man according to that which he had, to the poor, and the needy, and the sick, and the afflicted; and they did not wear costly apparel, yet they were neat and comely. And thus, in their prosperous circumstances, they did not send away any who were naked, or that were hungry, or that were athirst, or that were sick, or that had not been nourished; and they did not set their hearts upon riches; therefore they were liberal to all, both old and young, both bond and free, both male and female, whether out of the church or in the church, having no respect to persons as to those who stood in need.
Each gave according to what they had. They didn't turn anyone away. Their hearts weren't set on riches, so they could give freely.
